\subsection{External Checks}
\label{sec:exp-external}

LoCoBench is synthetic, and its gold follows our committee's reading. We therefore tested four of
the paper's claims on data that others built and labelled, with every prediction pre-registered
before any graph was mined (App.~\ref{app:external}). Both graph miners ran on every item. Claims
are sentences, except in QT30, where they are the corpus's propositions, and in GDTB, where they
are the two arguments of a relation. Table~\ref{tab:external} lists the hypotheses and their
outcomes.

\paragraph{Logical, not discourse, coherence.} On SummEval's \extSeN{} summaries, $\LCS$ is
uncorrelated with the experts' coherence ratings ($\rho=\extSeRhoCohGpt$ with GPT-6), as
predicted; the G-Eval judge correlates with them at $\extSeJudgeRhoCoh$. Under paragraph
permutation, the pre-registered comparison fails, but for an instructive reason. With GPT-6,
$\LCS$ stays within $\tau$ on \extLocoPermInvGpt\% of LoCoBench permutations, and re-mining the
unchanged text keeps it within $\tau$ on \extLocoNoiseInvGpt\%. On ContraDoc the two figures are
\extCdPermInvGpt\% and \extCdNoiseInvGpt\%. What moves $\LCS$ is the miner's sampling, not the
order of the text. The comparison fails because two of the discourse baselines cannot move at
all: RC and LC count repeated nouns regardless of order. The G-Eval judge, by contrast, falls on
\extLocoPermDecJudge\% of the permutations.

\paragraph{Conflicts in natural documents.} With every claim true, inserting a contradicting
sentence into a ContraDoc document lowers $\LCS$ on \extCdAssertDecGpt{} of \extCdPairs{} pairs
and raises it on \extCdAssertIncGpt{} (sign test $p<\extCdAssertPGpt$, GPT-6). The committee
confirms that \extCdSpotContradicted{} of the \extCdPairs{} inserted sentences are false given
the rest of their document. When they are read as false, a contradiction the miner found sets a
truth against a falsehood, which is a support. $\LCS$ then rises on \extCdVerdEdgeIncGpt{} and
falls on \extCdVerdEdgeDecGpt{} of the \extCdVerdEdgeNGpt{} pairs with such a contradiction:
the predicted direction, but not significant ($p=\extCdVerdEdgePGpt$). Recall is the
bottleneck. The miner finds the inserted contradiction in \extCdRecallInsertGpt\% of insertions,
but only \extCdRecallReplaceGpt\% of replacements, and hardly ever when the contradiction lies
within a single sentence (\extCdRecallIntraGpt\%), which no relation between two claims can
represent. The judge detects insertions more reliably: it falls on \extCdJudgeDec{} of
\extCdJudgeN{} pairs and never rises.

\paragraph{The sign follows the truth on real LLM output.} On ChatProtect's self-contradictions,
every relation the miner finds between the two sentences has the sign the theory predicts at
all four assignments of their truth values (\extCpSweepNGpt{} cases with GPT-6). The miner finds
the contradiction in \extCpConfStrongGpt\% of the pairs annotated as contradictory and in
\extCpConfNoneGpt\% of the others. With every claim true, adding the contradicting sentence lowers
$\LCS$ on \extCpAssertDecGpt{} pairs and raises it on \extCpAssertIncGpt{}. Where the annotators
recorded which side is false, \extCpRealSupportGpt{} of the \extCpRealSupportGpt{}+\extCpRealConflictGpt{}
contradictions found are supports at the real verdicts, because one or both sentences are false:
counting contradictions would charge every one of them.

\paragraph{The miner against human annotation.} On GDTB, the senses that compile to no coupling
receive one in \extGdNoneGpt\% of cases, against \extGdCorrectGpt\% correct couplings for the
senses that have one. Explicit relations are recovered more often than implicit ones
(\extGdExplicitGpt\% against \extGdImplicitGpt\%). On QT30's debates, where annotators reconstruct
implicit inferences that our miners are told not to emit, pair-level F1 is \extQtPairFGpt{}.
Inferences are recovered best (recall \extQtRecEntailmentGpt\%), rephrases are often read as
inferences, and conflicts between speakers are mostly missed (\extQtRecContradictionGpt\%).

Taken together, the score behaves as the theory says on natural text: it ignores discourse
organization, it falls when a text contradicts itself, and the sign of a relation follows the
truth. The binding constraint is relation extraction, above all the recall of conflicts.
